subject: How to check for resource availability before starting a trajectory?

messages.author: 532a72cafd4e6559
messages.subject: How to check for resource availability before starting a trajectory?
parts:
I am modeling a fleet of cars that have queue sizes of zero that are sent on delivery routes in pairs.  In my scenario the deliveries would not be sent if both cars were not available and the delivery trajectory would be skipped until the next scheduled time. 

 

What is the best way to check in advance for resource availability (here that two cars are available)?  Is there logic that can be added before the delivery trajectory, or do you backup and cancel the delivery trajectory if one or both cars are unavailable, some other option?

 

Any advice would be most appreciated.

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] How to check for resource availability before starting a trajectory?
parts:
Certainly, you have getters (get_server_count, get_queue_count...) to check the status of resources in advance, and you can use them in a trajectory to do this or that, or in a generator to plan the next arrivals. It is hard to say which way is better, because that depends on the specifics of your problem.

Iñaki

parts:
Thanks Iñaki! Could I ask for some more guidance here? How, for
example, would I create the logic complete or end the trajectory (and
wait for the next generator) if resources are not available?

I believe that I can get the available capacity using something like
the function below, but I’m not sure how to implement logic based on
it. Thank you!

function() {
# find available resources
capacities <- numeric(nrow(resources))
for (i in 1:length(capacities)) {
capacities[i] <- get_server_count(env, paste0("res_", resources$id[i]))
}
available <- ifelse(capacities == 0, T, F)
num_available <-sum(available)
enough <- ifelse (num_available > 1, T, F) ### here, defining
enough as having more than 1 available
return (c(enough))

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] How to check for resource availability before starting a trajectory?
parts:
I suggest you to read the documentation and, especially, the articles, where you'll find lots of examples and you'll familiarise yourself with the conventions and workflows. Then, you should be able to implement something very close to what you want to achieve, and then here we may help you with specific issues.

But I suspect you are new to R too, so I suggest you to start from the beginning with something like https://adv-r.hadley.nz/. Without a good grasp of base R, it would be very difficult to master simmer.

Iñaki
